title: SAE regularization produces more interpretable models
primary_claim: Adding an SAE loss term as a regularizer during LLM training (jointly training SAE layers alongside model weights) improves downstream SAE feature sparsity/reconstruction quality on nearly all layers of a small character-level GPT-2 model, without apparently harming overall model performance.
quote: We find that SAE regularization improves SAE performance on all layers and does not seem to impact the model's overall performance.
metric: cross-entropy loss increase at fixed SAE sparsity (L0~50)
target_value: SAE regularization reliably yields better (lower) cross-entropy loss increase on most layers; less dependable on some layers (e.g. layer 3); regularized models also reach slightly lower overall cross-entropy loss
tolerance_rationale: other scalar metric: 15% relative; post reported no spread, tolerance is a guess
inspector_notes: Fully self-contained toy reproduction: tiny in-repo data, no external model downloads, no gating. The five-step pipeline (train base GPT, train SAE-regularized GPT, sweep SAE loss coefficients on both, export results) is explicit in experiments/regularization/train.py and setup.py.
headline_artifact: experiments/regularization/results.sweep.json and results.sums.json (regularized vs. normal cross-entropy-loss-increase-at-fixed-L0 per layer), exported by train.py --step=4
